CnEVPost (2026-07-02) reports Deutsche Bank's Wang Bin attributing the June ES8 order decline to the phase-out of the RMB 10,000 purchase-tax subsidy plus customers waiting for the five-seat variant, and that DB still expected non-GAAP breakeven in Q2. Residual value: consensus is a $0.05/ADS loss while DB is at breakeven-to-positive, so a real non-GAAP profit print is still a live spread, which is why this is 78 and not 92.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the wire copy, and it is also double-counted. The Q2 miss was reported on 1-2 July across CnEVPost, Investing.com, TipRanks, MSN and the Deutsche Bank note syndication; the baseline records a -3.62% move on 2026-07-02, i.e. the price already paid for it. The hunter's own cited source, CnEVPost 2026-08-20, quantifies it to the unit: 'actual deliveries came in 2,342 units (-2.1%) below the low end.' Benzinga's 52-week-low piece names delivery softness and profitability concerns as the reason the stock is where it is. But the more serious problem is that 'consecutive disclosures' is one miss counted twice. NIO never issued a standalone June guide. April was 29,356 and May 37,705, so April+May = 67,061; the Q2 guide of 110,000-115,000 minus 67,061 gives 42,939-47,939 -- which is the claimed '42,900-47,900 June guide' rounded. The June figure and the Q2 figure are the same guidance range measured at two points, and a single 2.1% shortfall cannot be re-served as a pattern of impaired credibility. The claim's premise for a compounding discount factor therefore does not hold, on top of being fully published.

adversary_notes: Two claims in this brief are factually defective and one is self-cannibalising. (1) NIO-h1#4's 'consecutive disclosures' is a single guidance miss counted twice: April 29,356 + May 37,705 = 67,061, and the Q2 guide of 110,000-115,000 less 67,061 yields 42,939-47,939, which is the claimed '42,900-47,900 June guide'. There was no separate June guide to miss. (2) NIO-h1#0's central arithmetic is timing-inverted. The RMB 10,000 subsidy ran from March and covered orders locked through end-April/May per CnEVPost 2026-04-02, so most Q2 ES8 deliveries carried the cost; the withdrawal in June saves money on June-locked orders that deliver largely in Q3. The RMB 180m is not margin 'retained' inside the Q2 print, and the coincidence with Deutsche Bank's RMB 180m estimate is a collision of two different note vintages -- DB was at RMB 5m in the July note (per the Stocktwits/TradingView syndication I fetched) and RMB 180m in the August note. (3) NIO-h1#2's bottom-up August read is contradicted by the same outlet it is built on: CnEVPost 2026-08-28 has Onvo L60 at 3,201 units in the first 28 days of August against 4,949 in July, a ~35% fall, which makes 'flat-to-modestly-up sequentially' hard to sustain; if anything August prints below July. On the date-integrity warning: I verified every 2026 date from the URL path, and all five sources are genuinely 2026 -- the ES8 140,000/30-days piece (2026-08-21), the Onvo L60 110,000 piece (2026-08-28), the Ren Shaoqing pair (2026-08-21, 2026-08-24), the earnings-date piece (2026-08-20) and the analyst piece (2026-07-02) all resolve correctly. The 2025 base figures (July 21,017, August 31,305, September 34,749, Q3 87,071) are internally consistent and company-published, so I found no misdating in this brief. One structural point that suppresses everything here: the baseline's skew of -9.44 vol points, read with its own note ('positive = downside paid'), means the chain is paying more for calls than puts into a name sitting on a 52-week low after a -9.15% twenty-day drift. The market is not short of bad news on NIO; the bearish findings are arguing with the spot, and the bullish margin thesis is arguing with the option lean. Finally, the baseline's eight 'reactions' are monthly delivery reports, which the amendment correctly flags -- but that cuts both ways, because it also means this tape demonstrably repricing on delivery numbers is precisely why a 1 September delivery-plus-earnings-plus-guide stack is not a surprise to anyone holding the front straddle.
interactions: NIO-h1#0 and NIO-h1#4 rest on the same two documents (CnEVPost 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-20) and point in opposite directions from the identical fact -- #0 reads the 2.1% unit miss as margin bought, #4 reads it as credibility lost. They cannot both be marginal information. NIO-h1#2's 'compound catalyst' is stated verbatim inside NIO-h1#4's own cited source, which is the single strongest priced-in fact in this brief. And NIO-h1#2 is internally undercut by CnEVPost 2026-08-28, published three days before the print, which shows Onvo L60 down ~35% month-to-date rather than the flat-to-up the claim assumes.
